claim: Always serialize timestamps in UTC to avoid cross-region comparison bugs
rationale: prior incidents with mixed local/UTC timestamps in order ledger

claim: When sharing skills between Claude, Codex, and agentic-stack, prefer secondary registry lookup at the original skill root over symlink or copy mirrors.
rationale: User explicitly rejected hosting .agents skills under .claude/.codex; mirrors caused stale ownership and invalid skill drift.

claim: For CLI smoke tests, verify structured evidence that the model actually ran, such as nonzero Claude num_turns and duration_api_ms, instead of trusting exit code zero.
rationale: Claude CLI previously returned a successful process with zero turns/usage, causing a false negative/false pass during registry visibility testing.

claim: A config writer must locate its insertion point by parsing the structure, never by line offset from a matched key
rationale: skill_inventory_weekly.py inserted its tags: line at description_idx+1, which lands inside a 'description: >-' block scalar and corrupts the YAML frontmatter. 16 skills across three roots became unparseable over several weekly runs, and the inventory tool reported them as fine.

claim: A validator that finds the artifact it is meant to detect will report healthy; a self-inflicted corruption must be checked with an independent parser
rationale: get_frontmatter_tags searched for any line starting with 'tags:' and found the one the same script had just injected, so it declared the file healthy and the 16 broken skills never self-healed. Detecting with the same code path that wrote the data hides the bug indefinitely.

claim: An absent registry entry means unknown, not none; a maintenance job must never write a destructive default derived from missing metadata
rationale: The weekly tag writer filtered SOURCE_TAGS (custom/revised) out of the desired set and, finding no provenance entry, wrote 'tags: []' over 'tags: [custom]' on agent/paseo-help and agent/paseo-plugin. It reported the condition as a warning gap while performing the data loss as a write.

claim: launchctl bootstrap fails with 'Input/output error' when the label is marked disabled in launchctl print-disabled; run launchctl enable gui/<uid>/<label> first
rationale: Cost hours of misdiagnosis on 2026-09-28: the com.syang.agentic-stack.paseo-guard plist was valid, plutil-clean, and its script ran correctly by hand, yet load and bootstrap both failed with exit 5. launchctl print-disabled showed the label as 'disabled' from an earlier launchctl unload. The failure mode is indistinguishable from a broken plist, and the job is silently absent rather than erroring.

claim: A guard job must be tested against the failure shape it exists for, not only the shape seen when it was written
rationale: purge_paseo_duplicates.py only removed ~/.agents/skills/<name>/ when it contained a SKILL.md, and tried parents before children so a populated tree never collapsed. A live test with a bare directory and a stray file showed the retired root surviving a full 60s cycle — the exact condition the job exists to prevent. Also: a resident loop body under a StartInterval plist spawns a new process each interval.
